Hi Marissa,

We experienced a pretty disruptive incident this morning between ~01:10 - 03:45 UTC where our calls to Redwood's text-generation endpoint returned a mix of 5xx and 429s, plus client timeouts. Our service degraded — retries from our side only made things worse. We saw ~18% of requests fail or time out during the window; baseline is ~0.2%. This impacted order processing queues and a few customer-facing flows.

I’m attaching a quick summary from our side (error-sla-logs-20260226.csv) and a timeline. We need:
- a technical explanation for root cause
- exact request counts and error breakdown from Redwood for the same window
- confirmation on whether this constitutes an SLA breach and what credits you will provide

This is urgent. Please escalate to your engineering and customer success leads. We’ve already flagged legal because of the downstream revenue impact.

Samir

Marissa / Samir — preliminary engineering summary: 

What we observed:
- Time window: 2026-02-25T01:12:00Z — 2026-02-25T03:46:00Z.
- Error surface: ~14% 5xx (internal server errors) and ~4% 429 (rate-limited) across Veritas account keys during the peak.
- Root cause (initial): a client-side SDK change at Veritas triggered rapid retry bursts for a subset of endpoints. The repeated retries amplified load and caused queuing on a small number of inference hosts; one autoscaler policy mis-evaluated CPU headroom and did not spin up capacity fast enough, resulting in queue saturation and 5xx responses.

Mitigations applied (completed):
- Immediate throttling gate added to ingress for Veritas API key to cap retry amplification (01:40 UTC).
- Emergency scale-up of compatible model pools + temporary diversion to secondary region for read-only traffic (02:05 UTC).
- Rolling restart of three overloaded hosts (02:30 UTC).

Next steps:
- Full log correlation (request ids, token counts) and quantitative impact analysis (we will produce the per-minute error and latency series matched to your CSV). ETA: 48 business hours.
- Autoscaler policy changes and improved headroom heuristics.
- We'll produce an RCA and mitigation plan for preventing retry storms.

I’ve attached the raw error counts we exported (matching your CSV) for transparency.

—Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rohan — that helps. A few points:

1) Our internal logs show customer-impacting failures (payment processing delays) and a small number of SLA-level financial losses for three customers. We’ll need to quantify that but expect the figure to be material.

2) Per our contract (section 4.2), if a monthly availability drops below the guaranteed threshold, we’re entitled to service credits. We need a proposed credit calculation and timeline to settle.

3) We are also assessing whether to pause new feature rollouts that depend on the Redwood endpoint until this is closed.

Please treat the credit proposal as urgent — our procurement/legal teams are on standby.

Samir

Samir — following internal review I’m attaching a draft credit proposal (draft-credit-terms-v2.docx). High level:

- We acknowledge the incident window and the amplified effect from retry storms.
- Proposed commercial remedy: a one-time service credit equal to 20% of Veritas’s monthly usage for Feb 2026, plus two weeks of Dedicated capacity on us to help stabilize traffic patterns while you validate client SDK retries.
- We’re open to a different calculation if you provide a quantified list of direct losses tied to the incident.

Request: please confirm receipt and whether you are comfortable with this starting point. If yes, we’ll prepare a DocuSign with a short credit addendum and route for signatures. If no, please propose a counter-offer and any documentation you need.

I’m looping in Vivek since this bumps up to an executive exception.

Thanks,
—Marissa

Samir — thank you for your patience. Following engineering analysis and an internal exec review, here is our final offer to resolve the incident: 

1) Commercial credit: a one-time service credit equal to 20% of Veritas Health’s Feb 2026 Redwood usage, with a guaranteed floor of $45,000 (whichever is greater).
2) Operational support: two weeks of Dedicated capacity at no charge, plus a joint RCA workshop within 7 business days to review mitigation and long-term safeguards (retry throttles, autoscaler changes).
3) Implementation: we will prepare a short addendum to the Master Services Agreement and route via DocuSign. We will not include any admission of liability — language is limited to remedial credits and operational commitments as advised by legal.

Next steps for you: please indicate acceptance or propose a counter-offer by EOD Friday, 2026-03-06. If you accept, we’ll send the DocuSign and a HubSpot ticket will be created for the credit memo and Dedicated capacity setup.

Links: HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/ticket/VE-8902
